# The reasons a test may skip on the CI's cell: a hosted runner with a
# distribution kernel, no file capabilities and no GPU. One extended regular
# expression per line, matched against a skip line's text by
# .github/scripts/skip-gate.sh. Everything here is a privilege or a device the
# cell does not have; a workload the runner lacks is not here, because the
# workflow installs it.
#
# Adding a line is a claim about the cell. Say which, above the line.

# The capabilities the cell goes without, by name.
CAP_BPF|CAP_PERFMON|CAP_SYS_ADMIN|CAP_NET_RAW
# Unprivileged perf and bpf, as the tests word the kernel's refusal.
refuses unprivileged perf
will not (sample|count|open|report|read)
would not sample
refuses to sample another process
(cannot|may not|does not let this process) create a (bpf |task-storage )?map
does not let this process create the row maps
unprivileged_bpf_disabled
# tracefs, which is root's alone on a distribution kernel.
tracefs
# Hardware a cloud VM does not expose: an NVIDIA GPU, AMD IBS or Intel PEBS,
# RAPL, sensors, cpufreq, and hardware counters at all under some hypervisors.
nvidia|NVML|NVIDIA|GPU
# ... and a GPU's userspace, which a runner without one has no reason to carry:
# the CUDA driver library, and the Vulkan loader the fixtures link against.
fixture did not build, most likely because this machine has no -l(vulkan|:libcuda)
libcuda\.so\.1 is not loadable here
ibs_op|pebs|PEBS
RAPL
no /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl
temperature sensor
no chip under /sys/class/hwmon (publishes|reports) a temperature
# One hardware thread per core: a cloud vcpu is not a physical core's sibling.
no physical core here has two hardware threads
cpufreq
hardware counter|PMU|performance unit
# ... as the probe words it for a cpu that publishes no such event: a cloud
# VM's vcpu, which the CI's runner is (`ENOENT` at the open).
is not available on this cpu
# Sources this cell cannot serve. "no viable backend on this machine" is the
# resolver's own classification -- "the request is valid; it is this machine
# that cannot serve it" -- and the probes' reasons follow it on lines that a
# parallel suite's output interleaves with others, so the gate cannot always
# read them. The sweep of this cell (tests/portability.rs) is what checks that
# each of those reasons is a real one.
cannot serve
has no viable backend on this machine
needs what this machine does not grant
no backend of `[a-z_.]+` is usable here
serves neither backend
# Files the kernel keeps for root: powercap's energy counters.
root-only|readable only by root
# A cgroup controller the runner's service manager did not delegate to it.
is not delegated to
# ... or no cgroup at all: a cell that grants the capabilities and delegates
# no cgroup to this user, where a test that makes one below its own says so
# (tests/cli.rs, scenario_sched, scenario_proc).
no cgroup in this process's ancestry \(.*\) lets this user make one below it
# Counters a cpu does not have: top-down's issue slots (Intel from Icelake, AMD
# from Zen 4), a cache event the cpu does not publish.
this cpu (publishes no|has no) (slots|issue-slot)
does not open on this machine
# The machine's state at that moment, which the test cannot create and says so
# with its numbers: a shared runner's caches, its I/O stall, its huge pages.
# These are the "skip loudly with the numbers" scenarios; each wording is named
# so a new kind of state skip still stops the job.
caches were not this thread's
the second clean run was not clean
was already stalled on I/O
AnonHugePages moved from [0-9]+ to [0-9]+ huge pages
has no partially mapped huge pages right now
# The binary the cell builds carries no capabilities, as the workflow checks:
# a test with a privileged half says so by name (run 37f17c8, both cells).
carries no capabilities \(run `make`\)
# perf_event_paranoid 2 and above: page faults are sampled in user mode only
# (scenario_mem's kernel-mode half; both cells).
samples page faults in user mode only
# One matrix cell on disk, the runner's own: a gap between cells, or a cell
# that differs by a condition, needs two (tests/portability.rs).
matrix cell\(s\) under .*, and a gap needs two
no two cells of one machine differ by a condition the matrix sets
# The runner's vcpu count: a map sized for two cpus evicts nothing on two.
[0-9]+ cpus online, so a map of two holds every cpu
# No GPU: the one gpu source the cell serves has every backend written, so
# there is no unwritten one to pin.
gpu source\(s\) this machine serves have a collector for every backend
# The cloud disk's queue: a device the kernel's own `inflight` file never saw
# held long enough for a 20 ms gauge (scenario_io's queue-depth half; the
# spacing and volume halves still run).
skipped the depth: the kernel's own reads of /sys/block/[^/]+/inflight
# The runner's disk serving a cold 256 MiB file faster than `http.server`
# copies it, so the disk is not the request's time (cases/http-server-stdlib,
# `a-cold-file`'s `holds`; it skips on an NVMe too). The machine's storage,
# which the case cannot slow down without root.
a-cold-file/[a-z]+: the cause was not there to be found: .*the storage was slower than the server's copy
# A kernel whose root cgroup has no io.stat: `fs:cgroup` resolves onto nothing.
/sys/fs/cgroup/io.stat does not exist here
# The kernel's default ceiling (100 000/s) is at or above what this build can
# ask through the cpu clock, so nothing is throttled to assert on: the throttle
# half of scenario_cpu's ceiling test needs a lowered sysctl or the `pmu`
# collector (shown at paranoid 2 here, 2026-10-03).
perf_event_max_sample_rate is [0-9]+, at or above the [0-9]+ asked
